title: FIRST-TIME TESTER WALKTHROUGH
prompt: Prepare a friendly, task-based onboarding for a Gravity product tester. Program/version: [name]. Prior experience: [optional]. Test goals: [tasks]. Explain entry, safe sample data, expected checkpoints, how to report confusion or defects, and how to exit without exposing live restaurant records.
manager_check: Treat tester uncertainty as useful feedback, not as failure.

title: STRUCTURED TESTER ISSUE INTAKE
prompt: Transform a customer Testing Room submission into an actionable issue. Product/version/device: [details]. Steps and observed behavior: [text]. Evidence: [optional screenshot]. Separate defect, help request, design suggestion and unclear description; request only essential follow-up evidence.
manager_check: Do not collect passwords, PINs, employee secrets or unnecessary guest data.

title: TESTER SCREENSHOT PRIVACY CHECK
prompt: Review a proposed bug screenshot or screen recording: [description]. Identify names, schedules, wage rates, credentials, private recipes, customer information and hidden tabs that must be redacted. Recommend a replacement capture if safe masking would obscure the bug.
manager_check: Testing evidence is not permission to redistribute private data.

title: PRIVATE TESTER MESSAGE RESPONSE
prompt: Draft an accurate, respectful private reply to a tester: [issue or suggestion]. Confirm what was reported, state only verified behavior, ask a precise follow-up if needed and outline a realistic next validation step. Avoid promising a fix or publication that has not occurred.
manager_check: The reply should acknowledge evidence without overstating release status.

title: TESTER WALKTHROUGH REQUEST PLAN
prompt: Turn a request for a call or screen walkthrough into a short support agenda. User goal: [task]. Device, program version and obstacle: [facts]. Plan consent-based screen review, sample-data preparation, 3 key actions to demonstrate and a follow-up summary.
manager_check: Never ask a customer to reveal passwords or production-sensitive data on a call.

title: TESTER CONTRIBUTION AND PRIORITY REVIEW
prompt: Summarize tester contributions from [submission log, duplicates, severity, reproduction evidence and helpfulness notes]. Recognize actionable evidence, avoid rewarding praise over accuracy, and recommend follow-up testing areas without making unsupported promises of benefits.
manager_check: Recognition and rewards need documented, consistent criteria.

title: CUSTOMER PILOT EXIT DECISION
prompt: Evaluate whether a restaurant beta pilot should continue, expand or pause. Outcomes: [tested workflows]. Blockers, data integrity and user confidence: [facts]. Backup/restoration: [verified]. List open questions, approval owner and clear stop/go criteria.
manager_check: A passed automated test does not certify a customer environment.

title: RELEASE ARTIFACT VERIFICATION
prompt: Audit a candidate Windows release: [build commit, CI run, installer file, portable ZIP, checksums]. Match source, workflow evidence, size, integrity and expected runtime behavior; report any artifact mismatch or inaccessible download. Distinguish built, tested, uploaded and publicly released states.
manager_check: Do not call a private build artifact a public download.

title: EXE VERSUS PORTABLE ZIP INSTALLATION EXPLAINER
prompt: Write plain customer instructions for [Windows application/version]. Distinguish a setup installer (.exe) from a portable ZIP, explain where program data may live, show how to launch each, and warn against assuming a ZIP contains an INSTALL file.
manager_check: Instructions must match the exact files in the actual release.

title: WINDOWS UPGRADE DATA-CUSTODY CHECK
prompt: Plan a safe Windows beta update from [old version] to [new version] with [stored data and backups]. Identify data locations, export options, test restore, expected migration support and rollback plan. Explicitly mark unverified migrations and equipment compatibility.
manager_check: Preserve the prior working version until customer data is validated.

title: WORK STUDY GUIDED FREEZE REPRODUCTION
prompt: Investigate a Guided assistant freeze: [version, exact click sequence, logs and behavior]. Distinguish rapid repeat clicks, render/mutation loops, event registration, slow initialization and voice loading. Specify reproduction and regression tests; show a click-once instruction as support, not a substitute for an actual fix.
manager_check: A tooltip cannot replace a root-cause repair.

title: CEDAR VOICE AND OFFLINE TTS TEST PLAN
prompt: Design a desktop Guided voice acceptance test: [Windows app, microphone/speaker configuration, privacy consent, voice path]. Check the Cedar voice through its supported desktop process, not a broken site-relative file path. Separate TTS, transcription, offline behavior, permissions and audible-quality checks.
manager_check: Never claim device voice works based only on a source-code inspection.

title: PICTURE-LED USER MANUAL AUDIT
prompt: Audit a software manual against the actual program: [manual, build/version, screen captures]. Confirm each screenshot shows the same release, is readable in color and grayscale, matches control labels and contains no internal testing or private data. Identify missing numbered steps and outdated visuals.
manager_check: A screenshot of an older version may be worse than no screenshot.

title: PUBLIC DOWNLOAD PAGE PARITY AUDIT
prompt: Compare a website download page against published release assets: [page URLs, GitHub tag, filenames and checksums]. Check every button, installer/portable labels, update notes and support links. Flag stale pages and separately verify deployed production rather than assuming GitHub source equals the live site.
manager_check: A commit is not proof that production is updated.

title: RELEASE READINESS CUSTOMER SIMULATION
prompt: Run a customer-journey evaluation for [program/version]: download, extraction or installation, first launch, first task, Help, save/reopen, export, backup and uninstall/exit. Define test evidence, blocked steps, passing conditions and what remains a real-machine verification requirement.
manager_check: Customer readiness needs actual interaction, not only a successful build.

title: OWNER–GM DECISION AUTHORITY AGREEMENT
prompt: Help an owner and GM prepare a reviewable working agreement from [decision categories, limits, existing policy]. Distinguish owner-reserved decisions, delegated authority, emergency exceptions, communication timing, escalation and documentation; identify clauses requiring qualified legal or HR review.
manager_check: AI can structure an agreement but cannot approve or interpret legal obligations.

title: OWNER-ABSENCE CONTINUITY DECISION TREE
prompt: Prepare an owner-absence readiness plan for [restaurant, roles, contact chain, cash, safety and supplier scenarios]. Identify what the GM may handle, when to contact the owner, emergency authority, evidence to capture and reconnection steps.
manager_check: A continuity plan must name who has actual authority under existing policy.

title: MANAGER READINESS TRAINER-TRAINEE BOUNDARY
prompt: Review an instructor's trainee evaluation: [lesson, scenario response, observation and follow-up]. Distinguish teaching, coaching, employment discipline and actual certification authority. Propose a fair observation or reassessment without auto-promoting or punishing the trainee.
manager_check: Only qualified restaurant leadership makes readiness and employment decisions.

title: GRAVITY SIGNAL TO PROBLEM PROOF
prompt: Translate an aggregate operational signal into a Gravity investigation plan. Signal: [pattern]. Relevant records: [sources]. List multiple possible explanations, privacy boundaries, minimum proof and the owner who may authorize action. Do not infer guilt, intent or an individual performance issue.
manager_check: A signal is a question for management, not a verdict.

title: ONE-PROBLEM GRAVITY STARTER PATH
prompt: A restaurant has this immediate problem: [describe]. Available time, roles and tools: [facts]. Recommend the smallest useful Gravity method step, one standalone tool if appropriate, needed evidence, decision owner and verification checkpoint. Explain optional connections without pressuring a full-system adoption.
manager_check: Start with the customer's real problem, not a sales script.

title: WORKFLOW HANDOFF HISTORY AND READINESS
prompt: Assess readiness to move a case from Gravity Method to another Gravity workspace. Case history: [facts, decisions, owner and approvals]. Proposed transfer: [records]. Check provenance, missing prerequisites, unsupported assumptions, reversibility and retained accountability.
manager_check: A transfer must preserve decision history and never silently grant authority.

title: TWO-PER-WEEK GRAVITY REPORT EDITORIAL PLAN
prompt: Plan two useful Gravity Report articles each week from [verified restaurant questions, published books, existing tools and approved changes]. Group by leadership, staffing, inventory, SOP systems and ownership. For each article specify the real problem, evidence, corrective action, verification and a relevant optional resource.
manager_check: Avoid publishing invented customer stories or presenting unfinished tools as available.

title: NEWSLETTER TO FACEBOOK AND X ADAPTATION
prompt: Adapt this approved Gravity Report article for Facebook, X and a weekly email digest: [full article]. Preserve its practical voice, verified facts and useful takeaway while adjusting length, hook and link. Draft channel-specific copy without inventing testimonials, dates or past publication history.
manager_check: A scheduled post should not masquerade as an article published earlier.

title: WEBSITE CUSTOMER PROMISE CONSISTENCY
prompt: Audit these public website claims: [pages, product state, manuals, downloads and dates]. Compare announced features with verified live behavior and actual release files. Identify outdated counts, dead links, private-preview claims, security promises and copy needing a truthful correction.
manager_check: Customer copy must reflect production reality, not development intent.

title: FOUNDING YEAR RESOURCE NAVIGATION
prompt: Help a first-time Gravity visitor choose what to download or read. Their problem, restaurant size and preference for a standalone tool: [facts]. Offer a short relevant path, identify completed versus in-development resources, explain registration and Founding Year terms accurately, and leave the visitor free to stop after one useful resource.
manager_check: Access explanations must be accurate and non-coercive.
